title: MULTISENSOR MONITORING OF GROUNDWATER QUALITY AND SEISMIC ACTIVITY IN MOUNTAIN REGIONS

MULTISENSOR MONITORING OF GROUNDWATER QUALITY AND SEISMIC ACTIVITY IN MOUNTAIN REGIONS

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Yerik Alipuly, Zhansaya Dosymbekova, Samal Dosaibekova, Bulgyn Mailykhanova, Anvar Djalilov

ABSTRACT

This article proposes an industrial multisensor system based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) for continuous groundwater quality monitoring and seismological process control in mountainous regions. The system integrates a 3.2 km single-mode fiber-optic network, 640 spatial channels, a DAS interrogator operating in the 1-120 Hz frequency band, sensors for pH, electrical conductivity, total dissolved solids, oxidation–reduction potential, dissolved oxygen, turbidity, nitrate, and ²²²Rn, as well as an edge computer and a SCADA-level decision-making module. Validation was carried out using a 42-day pilot scenario, including a 14-day background period, an 18-day controlled impact period, and a 10-day post-impact period. Compared with point sensors, the system increased the probability of event detection from 0.76 to 0.94, improved specificity from 0.82 to 0.91, reduced false alarms from 0.23 to 0.11 per day, and decreased maintenance costs from 13.5 to 8.5 hours per month. When the integrated A(t) index exceeded the threshold of 1.25, the coordinated changes in DAS energy, radon, EC, and turbidity reliably distinguished hydroseismic anomalies. The results showed that the proposed system is relevant to the field of Industrial and Manufacturing Engineering, as it can be considered an industrially implementable, serviceable, scalable, and long-term monitoring-oriented solution.
